source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (the 4th Infantry assembled in the jungle west of the river while tanks tried to cross the sand bar, 23 October)
current_activity: attacking across the Matanikau sand bar with the coast force
engaged_note: 3rd Battalion, 1st Marines, holding the east bank (Miller, ch. VI)
notes: Miller, chapter VI: on 23 October 1942, after a heavy artillery preparation, nine medium tanks tried to cross the Matanikau sand bar while the 4th Infantry assembled in the jungle west of the river; no infantryman reached the east bank, and a second attempt farther upstream about midnight was halted. Confidence 0.5 (one US official family). The regiment is listed under the Sumiyoshi coast force in the same chapter.

notes: Miller, chapter VI, and Zimmerman: the 2nd Division’s October counter-offensive, 23–26 October 1942. Miller names the 4th, 16th and 29th Infantry among the regiments whose combat strength was reduced; Colonels Furumiya (29th) and Toshiro Hiroyasu (16th) were among the dead. Confidence 0.7.

current_activity: defending the Matanikau left bank against the American attack
notes: JACAR vol. 1, operations third period (C25080233100): on the morning of 1 November 1942 the enemy attacked the front of the 4th Infantry of the Sumiyoshi Detachment on the left bank of the Ma (Matanikau) River; on the 2nd the first line was pressed to the left bank of the Oki River. The claim date is 1 November, the first day of that action. Confidence 0.5 (one Japanese official family; a matching Miller sentence was not copied in this increment).
